correctness.rationale: The fixed, nonempty, named palette is essential: even a colour missing from the host is an admissible request. An extension type of a marked word is exactly a gap and a colour. Induct on depth: after choosing a witness, the two split gaps and all unchanged gaps need depth at least one less. This is equivalent to all old gaps satisfying the next-depth interval recurrence, since the unchanged gaps then already satisfy the lower threshold. At rank at least t+1, choose a depth-t witness pivot for each colour; the leftmost pivot guarantees a depth-t prefix, the rightmost a depth-t suffix, and their ordered list is an all-colour permutation. Conversely, each colour in an embedded central permutation has the prescribed witnesses on both sides by subsequence monotonicity. The base is the empty pattern at t=0. The grammar flattens to exactly 2^t−1 permutation blocks; every minimum word has those fixed boundaries, hence length q(2^t−1), multiplicity 2^t−1 for each colour and count (q!)^(2^t−1). All other rank-at-least-t hosts contain one, so the basis is minimal; the floor-log size bound is attained by extending a basis word. This verifies the marked formula, all-depth quantifiers, and q=1 and absent-colour conventions in RESULT.md lines 27–60. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed; no finite test is needed for the proved equivalence.

value.rationale: The exact identification converts an adaptive marked-gap game into a static word invariant. In particular one can count greedy full-alphabet arches in each gap in one scan, rather than enumerate game strategies or use the cubic interval dynamic program; taking floor log₂ of one plus the smallest gap count gives the rank. This explains not only the optimal size but which fixed-size hosts succeed, including missing-colour and non-extremal cases. The rank transfer is the substantive value; counting already-classified permutation concatenations alone would not qualify.
